channel.title: Elevate · The Entertrainer Blogs
channel.description: Articles about work, learning, technology, and the questions that stay with you.

item.title: You Are Not Lazy. You Are Helping the Universe Extend Its Life.
item.description: A small physics story about rest, hot tea, batteries, deleted files, and why the universe likes to spread things out. Read time: 8 minutes.

item.title: If you are an intelligent person, life might not be easy for you. Here’s why
item.description: Not because intelligence is a curse. Because a mind that can model more possibilities can also get stuck living in the model. Read time: 9 minutes.

item.title: Friend, friendly. Love, lovely. So why isn’t the Moon moonly?
item.description: English will build an adjective out of almost any noun, then quietly refuse for the Moon, the Sun and your own teeth. The reason is older than English. Read time: 7 minutes.

item.title: Does AI Understand You? Bloom’s Taxonomy Says Otherwise
item.description: An instructional designer walks the word “understand” through Bloom’s Taxonomy, and finds a very fast, very fluent machine that never quite arrives at the state the word describes. Read time: 10 minutes.

item.title: Why Staring at a Word Long Enough Can Make It Stop Being a Word
item.description: One evening at work I stared at the word "door" until it stopped looking like English. That glitch has a name, an Ig Nobel Prize, and a family of stranger cousins. Read time: 9 minutes.

item.title: The Midpoint of Your Life Isn't 40. It's 18.
item.description: A video I watched claimed the real midpoint of an 81-year life is age 18, not 40. The maths behind it is genuine, two centuries old — and shakier than the confident voiceover made it sound. Read time: 8 minutes.

item.title: The Voice in Your Head Is Not the Whole of You
item.description: That running commentary can rehearse a conversation, hold a phone number, and tell you not to send the message. Useful, yes. In charge of everything? Not quite. Read time: 9 minutes.

item.title: What It Would Take to Lie Perfectly
item.description: Perfect lying sounds like calm eyes and a locked story. Cognitive science suggests it is mostly a bandwidth problem — and that many imperfect lies succeed because listeners start in truth-default. Read time: 9 minutes.

item.title: You Are the Centre of the Universe — and Here’s Why
item.description: Space gets bigger between the galaxies — they are not walking. Hold anyone still and the sky runs away from them. Same for everyone. Read time: 8 minutes.

item.title: You Only Find Out You Don’t Know It When You Have to Explain It
item.description: The feeling of knowing arrives first, and cheaply. A zip, a policy, a search bar — they all sell you a working model. The model is often just a label with good lighting. Read time: 9 minutes.
